1. Backlog increased by 21% to its highest level since 2015, driven by offshore and international awards.
2. Full year free cash flow guidance was raised to between $70 million and $80 million, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow.
3. The company repurchased 5% of shares outstanding in Q3 and 8% year-to-date through September, totaling 966,000 shares for $21 million.
4. Net leverage ratio decreased to 1.3x, one quarter ahead of schedule, after reducing net debt by $12 million (nearly 10%) to $114 million.
5. Q3 consolidated EBITDA was $23 million, up 13% sequentially, with margins improving 150 basis points to nearly 12%.
6. Book-to-bill ratio was 122% consolidated, with the ROV product line achieving a book-to-bill ratio over 200%.
7. Coiled line pipe revenue grew 28% sequentially due to market share gains and revenue recognition on a Middle East project.
8. Facility consolidation from 4 plants to 2 is expected to contribute over $5 million of additional annualized cost savings by Q2 2026, bringing total structural savings to approximately $15 million.
9. Q4 2025 guidance projects revenue of $180 million to $200 million and EBITDA of $19 million to $23 million.
10. Management's FET 2030 plan targets doubling revenue organically over 5 years, with growth market share expansion from 8% to 16% expected to add $250 million in revenue in a flat market.

1. Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue was $168.5 million, representing 23% year-over-year growth and exceeding the high end of guidance by 7%.
2. Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $100.8 million with a 60% margin, beating the high end of guidance by 15%.
3. Free cash flow increased 37% year-over-year to $91.6 million in Q2.
4. Net revenue retention rate was 118% on a trailing 12-month basis.
5. The company had 121 customers contributing at least $500,000 each in subscription-based revenue (up 16% from 104 a year ago), accounting for 84% of total revenue.
6. AI tools quarterly active prescribers grew more than 50% from the prior quarter, while AI scribe quarterly active users nearly tripled versus Q1.
7. Multi-module integrated offerings represented over 40% of Q2 bookings compared to less than 5% in the same quarter last year.
8. SMB customer bookings grew roughly 100% year-over-year in Q2, driven by agency partner programs.
9. Full fiscal year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $640-646 million, representing 13% growth at the midpoint, with adjusted EBITDA guidance of $351-357 million at a 55% margin.
10. Telehealth platform now conducts over 300,000 voice and video visits on an average weekday, up from 200,000 previously announced.

1. Q3 2025 revenues were $377 million with gross profit of $66 million and net income of $22 million, representing the company's highest quarterly results since 2014.
2. Adjusted EBITDA was $104 million for Q3 2025, with positive operating cash flow of $24 million and positive free cash flow of $23 million.
3. The company had cash and cash equivalents of $338 million and total liquidity of $430 million at quarter end, with funded debt of $315 million resulting in negative net debt of $31 million.
4. Full-year 2025 guidance was tightened to revenues of $1.23 billion to $1.29 billion, EBITDA of $240 million to $270 million, and free cash flow of $100 million to $140 million.
5. Year-to-date share repurchases totaled $30 million with 4.6 million shares acquired, in line with the target of minimum 25% of expected free cash flow.
6. The company executed a 3-year well intervention contract with a minimum 150-day commitment for key units in the Gulf of America.
7. The Q7000 completed a 400-day decommissioning campaign for Shell in Brazil with 100% utilization, and continues working for Shell into Q2 2026.
8. Shallow water abandonment segment utilization increased to 790 days in Q3 compared to 614 days in Q2, with the Hedron heavy lift barge achieving 100% utilization.
9. Both Siem Helix vessels in Brazil are due for 5-year special surveys in 2026, which management stated will meaningfully impact anticipated EBITDA improvements.
10. The company entered a 4-year agreement with NKT for installation, operation, project engineering and maintenance of the T3600, designed to be the world's most powerful subsea trencher.

1. Bel Fuse delivered record full year 2025 net sales of $675.5 million, a 26.3% increase over 2024, with Q4 sales of $175.9 million up 17.4% year-over-year.
2. Full year 2025 gross margin expanded to 39.1% (from 37.8% in 2024), with Q4 2025 gross margin reaching 39.4% (up from 37.5% in Q4 2024).
3. Aerospace and defense accounted for 38% of consolidated 2025 sales, with 28% from defense and 10% from commercial aerospace.
4. The company paid down $90 million in long-term debt during 2025, leaving $197.5 million of total debt outstanding at December 31, 2025, with a weighted average interest rate of 4.4%.
5. Full year 2025 book-to-bill ratio was 1.1, strengthening to 1.3 in Q4 2025 with strength across all three product segments.
6. Q1 2026 guidance calls for sales of $165 million to $180 million with gross margin expected in the range of 37% to 39%, reflecting anticipated headwinds from higher material costs and unfavorable FX.
7. On an organic basis, 2025 sales grew by $41.5 million or 7.8% over 2024, with all three product segments delivering organic growth in Q4.
8. Power Solutions Q4 2025 gross margin was 44.5%, a 390 basis point improvement from Q4 2024, driven by higher aerospace and defense sales, favorable product mix, and better fixed cost absorption.
9. AI-specific customer sales in the Power segment reached $4 million in Q4 2025, up from $3.3 million in Q4 2024, with networking and AI cited as continued growth drivers into 2026.
10. Full year 2025 cash flows from operations were $80.6 million, with the company planning to continue quarterly debt paydowns of $20 million to $30 million barring M&A activity.

1. Neogen delivered Q1 revenue of approximately $209 million, up 0.3% year-over-year on a core basis, which was in line with expectations.
2. The company executed a global headcount reduction of approximately 10% of existing and planned positions, expected to reduce operating expenses by approximately $20 million on an annualized basis.
3. Adjusted EBITDA was $35.5 million in Q1, representing a margin of 17%, down from prior year due to lower volume, gross margin headwinds, and higher operating expenses.
4. Petrifilm, which has had a core revenue CAGR in the mid-single-digit range over recent years, experienced a mid-single-digit decline in Q1 attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing.
5. Q1 free cash flow was an outflow of $13 million, representing an improvement of $43 million compared to the prior year Q1.
6. The company completed the divestiture of its cleaners and disinfectants business for approximately $115 million in net proceeds, using $100 million to pay down debt with annualized interest savings of roughly $6 million.
7. Neogen ended Q1 with gross debt of $800 million (68% at fixed rate) and a total cash position of $139 million.
8. Food Safety segment revenues were $152 million, down 4.6% compared to prior year including a core decline of 1.7%, while Animal Safety segment revenues were $57 million with core revenue growth of 5.8%.
9. The company expects to realize approximately $12 million benefit from cost reduction actions this fiscal year, with more than half already contemplated in initial guidance.
10. Adjusted earnings per share were $0.04 in Q1 compared to $0.07 in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower adjusted EBITDA which more than offset lower interest expense.

1. Q3 2025 revenue was $1.6 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with operating EBITDA of $100 million, down $8 million versus prior year.
2. Q3 closed transaction volume increased 7%, marking the first growth in units since Q4 2024 and outperforming NAR's volume growth by over 2 percentage points.
3. Luxury segment delivered 12% year-over-year volume growth, with 345 homes priced $10 million or higher sold in Q3, representing a 30% increase from the prior year.
4. The company realized $67 million in cost savings year-to-date and is on target to achieve $100 million in cost savings for 2025, with 100% of savings already identified.
5. Q3 free cash flow was $92 million, down $7 million year-over-year, primarily due to increased capital expenditures supporting AI transformation initiatives.
6. The company reduced its revolver balance by $195 million in Q3 to $415 million and has no significant note maturities until 2029.
7. Advisors agent retention reached nearly 95% among the top half of producing agents in Q3, among the highest rates ever achieved.
8. October momentum continued with closed volume up 9% and open volume up 6%, both showing growth in transaction units.
9. Operating EBITDA was negatively impacted by a $16 million year-over-year increase in employee long-term cash incentive costs as the stock price nearly tripled during the quarter.
10. The proposed merger with Compass is expected to close in the second half of 2026, subject to shareholder approval and regulatory approvals, and the company has suspended forward guidance.

1. Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales were $341.3 million, a 5% decrease year-over-year.
2. Medical vertical sales were $96 million in Q2, up 15% year-over-year, representing the fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth in that vertical.
3. Fiscal 2026 net sales guidance was raised to $1.4 billion to $1.46 billion from the prior range of $1.35 billion to $1.45 billion, driven by Medical strength and European Automotive program ramps.
4. Adjusted operating income guidance was raised to 4.2% to 4.5% of net sales versus the prior estimate of 4.0% to 4.25%.
5. Gross margin rate improved 160 basis points year-over-year to 8.2% from 6.6%, driven by favorable mix, the Tampa facility closure, favorable FX, and restructuring efforts.
6. Borrowings at December 31, 2025, were $154 million, down approximately 25% or $51 million from a year ago.
7. Nexteer represented 20% of sales in the December quarter, up from 19% in the September quarter.
8. The new Indianapolis medical CMO facility is 300,000 square feet and is expected to drag on margins for the next 2 to 3 quarters due to depreciation and dual-facility operating costs before becoming accretive.
9. Automotive sales of $162 million declined 13% year-over-year, but the company expects Q3 Automotive to be flat to slightly up as it finally anniversaries the EB100 braking program transfer.
10. The company repurchased 149,000 shares for $4.3 million in Q2, with $10.5 million remaining on the Board-authorized share repurchase program.

1. Fiscal Q1 2026 revenue was $381 million, representing a 1% increase compared to $376 million in the prior year period.
2. New Boat sales were down 6% compared to the prior year while Pre-Owned Boat sales were 24% higher, driven by both increased unit sales and average unit price.
3. Gross profit margin expanded to 23.5%, an improvement of 110 basis points compared to the prior year quarter.
4. The company recognized a $7 million impairment charge related to certain distribution assets classified as held for sale.
5. Net loss for the quarter totaled $8 million or $0.47 per diluted share compared to a net loss of $14 million or $0.81 per diluted share in the prior period.
6. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $4 million compared to $2 million in the prior year.
7. Total inventory decreased to $602 million as of December 31, 2025, compared to $637 million as of December 31, 2024.
8. Net debt represents 5.1x trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA, with the company expecting leverage to drop to almost 4x by end of March quarter and under 4x by year-end following distribution asset sale.
9. The company is maintaining FY2026 guidance with total sales expected in the range of $1.83 billion to $1.93 billion and adjusted EBITDA in the range of $65 million to $85 million.
10. Management expects New Boat margins to improve by 100 basis points for the full year while the industry is expected to be flat to down low single digits year-over-year.

1. Kontoor Brands returned over $140 million to shareholders in 2025 through dividends and share repurchases, and generated over $450 million of cash from operations for the full year.
2. Helly Hansen's China joint venture generated revenue of approximately $100 million in 2025, increasing 95% compared to prior year, with another year of strong growth expected north of 50% in 2026.
3. Full year 2026 adjusted EPS is expected to be in the range of $6.40 to $6.50, representing an increase of 15% to 16%, with full year revenue expected between $3.40 billion and $3.45 billion.
4. The gross tariff impact for 2026 remains over $100 million, with 160 to 180 basis points of pressure on gross margin net of mitigating actions, and the company expects to fully offset tariffs within 12 to 18 months.
5. Project Jeanius delivered gross savings of over $50 million in 2025 and is expected to approach $100 million of gross savings in 2026, reaching full run rate in the second half of 2026.
6. Helly Hansen synergies have been identified at more than $40 million, up from the prior $25 million target, with full run rate expected in 2027.
7. Total inventory decreased by $198 million or 26% sequentially in Q4, exceeding the plan by $78 million, and Helly Hansen's inventory days outstanding were reduced by approximately 100 days compared to prior year.
8. The company anticipates returning to less than 1.5x net leverage by the end of 2026, with voluntary term loan payments of $225 million planned, bringing total acquisition-related debt repayments to $475 million or approximately 70% of the total debt incurred for Helly Hansen.
9. Wrangler's men's and women's bottoms business delivered its 15th consecutive quarter of market share gains as measured by Circana, with full year global revenue increasing 4% driven by double-digit growth in female, Western, and DTC.
10. Helly Hansen contributed $0.44 per share in Q4 versus prior outlook of $0.29, with Q4 earnings exceeding the company's outlook by more than 50%, and the company expects Helly to deliver mid- to high single-digit revenue growth in 2026 with low-teen operating earnings growth.

1. Q4 2025 revenue grew to $1.095 billion, up 7% year-over-year as reported and 6% in constant currency, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.84, up 11% year-over-year.
2. Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) Q4 revenue was $94 million, up 45% year-over-year, accelerating from 39% growth in Q3, and now represents approximately 50% of total compute revenue.
3. Akamai signed a 4-year, $200 million commitment for Cloud Infrastructure Services with a major U.S. tech company, with a large majority of spend for AI Inference Cloud and revenue recognition expected to begin in Q4 2026.
4. API Security grew by more than 100% year-over-year, exiting the year with a revenue run rate exceeding $100 million, with less than 10% penetration among existing customers.
5. Akamai plans to invest approximately $250 million in CapEx in 2026 to augment its AI Inference Cloud, while also facing approximately $200 million in additional CapEx costs due to significant inflationary pressure in memory chip and server pricing.
6. Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $4.4 billion to $4.55 billion (up 5% to 8% as reported), with non-GAAP EPS expected in the range of $6.20 to $7.20.
7. CIS revenue growth is projected to accelerate to 45% to 50% year-over-year in 2026, with momentum building in the second half driven by the scaling of AI Inference Cloud.
8. Full year 2026 non-GAAP operating margin is estimated at approximately 26% to 28%, declining from 29% in Q4 2025, mainly due to increased colocation and depreciation expense from the CIS build-out.
9. In full year 2025, Akamai spent $800 million to repurchase approximately 10 million shares, marking the largest annual buyback in company history, with cash and marketable securities totaling approximately $1.9 billion as of December 31.
10. The initial AI Inference Cloud deployment across 20 cities is already sold out from beta customers, and Akamai plans to increase capacity by approximately an order of magnitude using the $250 million investment.

1. Biofrontera delivered record annual revenues of $41.7 million in 2025, representing approximately 12% growth over the prior year.
2. Fourth quarter 2025 revenues were $17.1 million, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, representing approximately 36% year-over-year growth.
3. The new earn-out structure with Biofrontera AG reduced cost of revenues per unit to about 15%, replacing a transfer pricing model that previously ranged from 25% to 35% of revenue, improving Q4 gross profit margin from approximately 58% to 82%.
4. Adjusted EBITDA for Q4 2025 was $4.9 million compared to negative $1.4 million in Q4 2024, with an adjusted EBITDA margin improving to positive 29% from negative 11%.
5. The FDA accepted the supplemental NDA filing for superficial basal cell carcinoma with a PDUFA target action date of September 28, 2026, based on Phase III data showing 76% complete histological clearance versus 19% for placebo.
6. Full year 2025 net loss narrowed to $10.5 million from $17.8 million in 2024, a reduction of approximately 41%.
7. Management expects long-run gross profit margins to range between 80% and 85%, with the full benefit of the new cost structure to be realized on an annualized basis in 2026.
8. Ameluz full year 2025 unit volume reached approximately 121,000 tubes, representing approximately 10% volume growth over 2024, with Q4 volumes of approximately 49,840 tubes.
9. The company secured $11 million in funding through a private placement of Series C preferred stock and received $3 million from the initial Xepi divestiture closing, with potential for up to an additional $7 million in milestone payments.
10. The Phase II acne vulgaris trial showed a 58% reduction in inflammatory lesions with Ameluz versus 37% with vehicle gel, with 86% patient satisfaction, and the company plans to discuss Phase III design with the FDA in Q3 2026.

1. REGENXBIO ended Q3 2025 with cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $302 million, up from $245 million at December 31, 2024.
2. The company expects its September 30 cash balance to fund operations into early 2027, with multiple nondilutive financing opportunities that could extend runway well beyond 2027.
3. RGX-202 pivotal trial enrollment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy has been completed ahead of original year-end guidance, with top-line data expected in early Q2 2026 and BLA submission planned for mid-2026.
4. RGX-121 for MPS II has a PDUFA date of February 8, 2026, and FDA completed inspections of clinical sites and the in-house manufacturing facility with no observations.
5. The company's wet AMD Phase III studies (ATMOSPHERE and ASCENT) completed enrollment with over 1,200 patients across 200 sites, representing the largest global gene therapy program ever conducted.
6. Top-line data for the subretinal wet AMD program is expected in Q4 2026.
7. REGENXBIO's manufacturing facility contains a 2,000-liter bioreactor capable of producing up to 2,500 doses of RGX-202 per year.
8. Q3 2025 revenues were $30 million compared to $24 million in Q3 2024, with the increase primarily due to development service revenue under the Nippon Shinyaku partnership.
9. The AbbVie collaboration includes a $100 million milestone payment for the diabetic retinopathy program upon first patient dose.
10. RGX-202 has demonstrated no SAEs or adverse events of special interest in Phase I/II, including no thrombocytopenia or liver injury, with product purity exceeding 80% full capsids.

1. QuickLogic was awarded a $13 million tranche for its ongoing U.S. government contract, with revenue recognition beginning in Q1 2026.
2. Q4 2025 total revenue was $3.7 million, down 35% from Q4 2024 and up 84% from Q3 2025.
3. Q1 2026 total revenue guidance is $5.5 million (plus or minus 10%), representing nearly 50% sequential growth from Q4 2025.
4. The company forecasts full year 2026 revenue growth of between 50% and 100% over fiscal 2025.
5. Non-GAAP gross margin in Q4 2025 was 20.8%, negatively impacted by $473,000 in inventory reserves and $135,000 in unanticipated contracted professional services costs.
6. Full year 2026 non-GAAP gross profit margin is modeled at 57%, with Q1 and Q2 expected around 45% and significant improvement in Q3 and Q4.
7. Total cash at the close of Q4 was $18.8 million (inclusive of $15 million from the credit facility), with $3.2 million raised via ATM during Q4 and another approximately $3.2 million raised via ATM during Q1 2026.
8. The U.S. government contract ceiling has expanded to a potential $89 million, with GlobalFoundries' 12LP fabrication process added to the program.
9. Management expects Q1 2026 to be the revenue low point for the year, with the company expected to be both cash flow positive and net income positive in the second half of 2026.
10. Three multi-project wafer tape-outs are planned for 2026 for storefront products, with costs of two fully covered by customer contracts and the third expected to be at least partially covered.

1. Organogenesis delivered Q4 2025 record net product revenue of $225.1 million, up 78% year-over-year and 50% sequentially, exceeding the high end of the guided range of $162 million to $187 million by approximately $50 million at the midpoint.
2. Advanced Wound Care net product revenue grew 83% year-over-year to $217.2 million in Q4 2025, driven by better-than-expected growth.
3. Surgical & Sports Medicine product revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $7.9 million in Q4 but grew 12% for the full year 2025.
4. Q4 2025 gross profit margin was 78% of net product revenue, up from 75% in the prior year period, primarily due to a shift in product mix.
5. Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $84.2 million, or 37% of total revenue, compared to $18.2 million, or 14% of total revenue, in the prior year period.
6. The company expects total net revenue to decline 25% to 38% year-over-year for full year 2026, with Q1 2026 revenue expected to decline approximately 50% year-over-year due to clinician confusion from CMS' December 30 commentary on discarded products.
7. Management expects first half 2026 revenue declines of approximately 30% to 35%, with strong sequential growth in Q2, Q3, and Q4, and expects high teens adjusted EBITDA margins in Q4 2026.
8. As of December 31, 2025, the company had $94.3 million in cash with no outstanding debt, down from $136.2 million a year earlier, plus availability of up to $75 million under a revolving credit facility.
9. The company initiated a rolling BLA submission for its ReNu knee osteoarthritis program in late 2025 and expects to complete it in the first half of 2026, which management described as a transformational opportunity.
10. Organogenesis commercialized Dermagraft, adding another PMA product to its portfolio, and is advancing a new manufacturing and R&D center in Smithfield, Rhode Island to scale production of Apligraf and PuraPly AM and support potential burns products FortiShield and TransCyte.

1. Total worldwide revenue for Q3 2025 was $21.5 million, a 5% increase from $20.4 million in Q3 2024 (4% on a constant currency basis).
2. U.S. revenue in Q3 2025 was $14 million, only a 1% increase from $13.8 million in the prior year period.
3. International revenue for Q3 2025 was $7.5 million, a 15% increase year-over-year (9% on a constant currency basis).
4. The company added 9 new U.S. centers during the third quarter.
5. Gross margin for Q3 2025 was approximately 75%, compared to 74% in Q3 2024.
6. Research and development expenses increased 29% year-over-year to $4.8 million in Q3 2025.
7. The company ended Q3 2025 with $76.5 million in cash and cash equivalents, a decrease of $7.7 million from Q2 2025.
8. Total cash utilization for the first three quarters of 2025 was approximately $25 million.
9. Full year 2025 revenue guidance was updated to $89 million to $90 million.
10. Full year 2025 operating expense guidance is $125 million to $126 million, inclusive of approximately $21 million in noncash stock-based compensation.

1. Glo Fiber reached 400,000 homes and businesses passed at end of Q3, with 21,000 homes released to sales in the quarter.
2. Glo Fiber data revenue-generating units grew 39.5% year-over-year to 83,000 customers, while Glo Fiber revenues increased 41.1% to $21.3 million.
3. Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.7% year-over-year to $29.7 million, with margins expanding 300 basis points to 33%.
4. The company remains on track to reach positive free cash flow for the full year 2027, driven by declining capital intensity and continued customer growth.
5. 92% of Glo Fiber passings are in duopoly markets with only one fixed broadband competitor.
6. Liquidity stood at $213 million on September 30, with $535 million of outstanding debt and the first material maturity in July 2027.
7. The company expects 2025 revenues of $352 million to $357 million and adjusted EBITDA of $113 million to $118 million.
8. Earliest Glo Fiber cohorts from 2019-2020 have reached an average data penetration rate of 37%, with typical penetration of 15% in year one and 25% by year three.
9. Following the introduction of new promotional rate plans with a 5-year price guarantee, 68% of new residential customers chose speeds of 1 gig or higher.
10. The company expects data ARPU to decline approximately 1% for 2026 as more customers select new promotional plans.

1. Etsy signed a definitive agreement to sell Depop to eBay for $1.2 billion in cash, with the transaction expected to close in Q2 2026.
2. Consolidated Q4 GMS was $3.6 billion, up 2.4% year-over-year excluding Reverb, and consolidated revenue was a record $882 million, up 6.6% excluding Reverb.
3. Etsy marketplace GMS was up 0.1% year-over-year in Q4, the first positive comparison since Q3 2023, with U.S. buyer GMS growing 0.3% for the first time in 4 years.
4. Q1 2026 GMS guidance is $2.38 billion to $2.43 billion (approximately 2% to 4% year-over-year growth), with a take rate of approximately 25.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin between 28% and 30%.
5. Management expects slight full-year 2026 GMS growth with positive year-over-year comparisons in each quarter, noting Q1 may be the strongest due to currency tailwinds and favorable comparisons.
6. Agentic traffic to Etsy in Q4 was approximately 15x what it was a year ago, though it remains less than 1% of total traffic, with higher average order values compared to mature acquisition channels.
7. In 2025, Etsy generated $735 million in adjusted EBITDA, converted approximately 87% to free cash flow, and returned more than 100% of free cash flow to shareholders through $777 million in share repurchases that reduced the share count by 14.4 million shares.
8. The app's contribution to total GMS reached 46% in Q4, up 5 percentage points from end of 2023, with app GMS growth accelerating to 6.6% year-over-year and app users showing 40% higher lifetime value than non-app users.
9. Depop generated $1.1 billion in GMS and $187 million in revenue for full year 2025, with Q4 GMS up nearly 38% year-over-year to a record $300 million and U.S. GMS growing 60%.
10. Etsy added 6.8 million new buyers and reactivated 10.4 million lapsed buyers in Q4, totaling 17.2 million gross additions, up 2.7% year-over-year and growing for the first time in over 2 years.

1. Q3 2025 revenue increased 115% year-over-year to $30.6 million, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth.
2. U.S. sales grew approximately 68% sequentially, making it Tigo's largest sales region on a country level for the quarter.
3. Gross profit margin improved to 42.7% in Q3 2025 compared to 12.5% in the prior year period.
4. The company returned to GAAP operating profitability with operating income of $0.6 million, compared to an operating loss of $10.4 million in the prior year period.
5. Adjusted EBITDA increased to positive $2.9 million in Q3, compared to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $8.3 million in the prior year period.
6. Principal on convertible debt due in early January 2026 is $50 million, and the company expects to complete refinancing in Q4 2025.
7. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term and long-term marketable securities totaled $40.3 million at September 30, 2025.
8. Q4 2025 guidance projects revenues between $29 million and $31 million, representing a flat quarter versus the typically seasonally slow period.
9. Full year 2025 revenue guidance is between $102.5 million and $104.5 million.
10. Management stated they feel comfortable that gross margins of 40-plus percent will remain steady through 2026.

1. Full year 2025 EPS excluding notable items was $10.30, up 19% year-over-year, while Q4 EPS grew 14% year-over-year.
2. Assets under custody/administration reached a record $53.8 trillion, up 16% year-over-year, surpassing $50 trillion for the first time in 2025.
3. Assets under management hit an all-time high of $5.7 trillion, up 20% year-over-year, with Q4 net inflows of $85 billion.
4. For 2026, management expects fee revenue growth of 4% to 6%, NII growth in the low single digits, and expense growth of approximately 3% to 4%.
5. The company achieved $500 million in productivity savings in 2025 and is targeting a comparable level of savings in 2026.
6. Private markets servicing fees grew 12% in 2025 and now represent approximately 10% of total servicing fees, up from 9% in 2024.
7. Return on tangible common equity was 20% for full year 2025 excluding notable items, with Q4 reaching 22%.
8. Pretax margin expanded by more than 150 basis points in 2025 to approximately 29%, with management targeting roughly 30% for full year 2026.
9. The company returned over $2.1 billion in capital to shareholders in 2025 and expects a total payout ratio of roughly 80% in 2026.
10. Net interest margin expanded to 1.10% in Q4 2025, up 3 basis points year-over-year, with management expecting continued NIM improvement in 2026.

1. Q3 2025 bookings came in at $15.5 million TCV, approximately 20% below internal expectations, compared to $25.6 million sequentially and $21 million year-over-year.
2. Adjusted EBITDA margins are expected to expand approximately 600 basis points from 2023 to year-end 2025.
3. The company has paid down debt by approximately $35 million since January 2024, reducing net leverage ratio from 4.4x in Q4 2023 to 2.2x in Q3 2025.
4. Year-to-date free cash flow improved by $20 million compared to the corresponding period, with cash balance growing from $3.8 million at end of 2023 to approximately $20 million today.
5. Financial health bookings in the 100-400 bed hospital space increased from less than 20% in 2024 to more than 30% in 2025.
6. Q3 2025 total revenue was $86.1 million, up approximately 2% year-over-year, with recurring revenue at approximately 94% of total revenue.
7. Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $16.3 million with an 18.9% margin, representing a 155 basis point improvement compared to Q3 2024.
8. Patient Care gross margin expanded to approximately 60% in Q3, an increase of nearly 370 basis points versus last year.
9. Full year 2025 guidance includes revenue of $345-$348 million and adjusted EBITDA of $65-$68 million, with Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin expected around 20% at the midpoint.
10. The company expects to deliver approximately 200 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in 2026 from the midpoint of full year 2025 guidance, driven by cost optimization and global offshore transition savings.

1. Cineverse reported Q3 fiscal 2026 revenues of $16.3 million, down from $40.7 million in the prior year quarter which included over $20 million in Terrifier 3 theatrical results.
